chase.description: Chase checking export — no category column (all rows will soft-fail to 'Other'/Unchecked), has 'Balance' and 'Check or Slip #' columns that must be dropped, expense-negative amounts.

plan.column_map_reasoning: The 'Posting Date' clearly maps to posted_date. 'Description' contains transaction details and merchant names, so it maps to description. 'Amount' is the transaction value. 'Type' appears to hold transaction type/category information, so it maps to primary_category. 'Details', 'Balance', and 'Check or Slip #' don't map cleanly to Budgy schema fields — 'Balance' is an account balance (informational, not a transaction field), 'Check or Slip #' is an identifier that doesn't fit the schema, and 'Details' is unclear. These are mapped to null.
plan.category_map_reasoning: All unique category values are merchant names and transaction descriptions rather than categorical labels. Each has been mapped to the most specific Budgy category based on the merchant type: e.g., Amazon → Shopping/Retail, Shell Oil → Transportation/Gas & EV charging, Direct Deposit → Income/Wages, CVS → Health & wellness/Pharmacy, Uber → Transportation/Taxi & ride shares, Venmo → Transfers/Person to person payments, Target → Shopping/Retail, Starbucks → Food & drink/Coffee shops, Chipotle → Food & drink/Restaurants & bars, Landlord → Housing & utilities/Rent, Spotify and Netflix → Services/Digital services, Con Edison → Housing & utilities/Gas & electricity, Planet Fitness → Health & wellness/Fitness, Whole Foods → Food & drink/Groceries.
plan.amount_transform_reasoning: All sample Amount values are either negative (expenses: -87.43, -6.75, -42.5, -15.99, -58.2, -45.0, -110.0, -23.18, -18.5) or positive (income: 3200.0). The presence of a positive 3200.0 value alongside many negative values, combined with the merchant data (DIRECT DEP PAYROLL suggests income), indicates that expenses are represented as negative numbers and income as positive. This follows the standard 'expense_negative' convention, so no transformation is needed.
